detail: No express derivatives rule. Creating a derivative over Securities, and buying or selling financial products created over or in respect of Securities, are Dealings; Securities includes derivatives and any financial product with no venue limit, so an OTC put/call is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance and is barred in Closed Periods, Additional Prohibitions and while holding Inside Information.
evidence: buy or sell Securities or financial products issued or created over, or in respect of Securities ... create a derivative over Securities

detail: Absolute ban on instruments limiting economic risk of equity incentive scheme securities while subject to performance hurdles or otherwise unvested.
evidence: You must not Deal in instruments or other financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of any Securities issued to you under any equity incentive schemes provided by Origin while those holdings are subject to performance hurdles or are otherwise unvested.

detail: Hedging arrangements over vested plan securities are expressly contemplated and must comply with the Policy, i.e. prior written clearance, outside Closed Periods/Additional Prohibitions, no Inside Information. The policy does not distinguish vested-but-locked shares; hedging of non-plan shares is not named and is caught only as a Dealing.
evidence: Any sale, hedging arrangement or other Dealing involving those Securities after they have vested must be done in compliance with this Policy.

detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a Dealing (financial product in respect of Securities; agreement to sell) requiring clearance. Any monetisation that takes security over Origin Securities is a secured financing arrangement prohibited by 7.1.
evidence: enter into an agreement to do any of the above, and Deal has a corresponding meaning.

detail: Outright ban; short selling is also listed within the Dealing definition as a short-term trade.
evidence: You must not engage in short-selling Origin Securities.

detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed in the Dealing definition.

CFDs are not named. They are financial products in respect of Securities and so a Dealing requiring clearance, but a CFD would in practice fall within the ban on short-term or speculative Dealing and, if short, the short-selling ban.
evidence: You must not Deal in Origin’s Securities on a short-term or speculative basis.

detail: Margin loans using Origin Securities as collateral, solely or as part of a portfolio, are banned from the date of the Policy. A lender's forced sale in a Closed Period or other prohibited time is a serious breach.
evidence: From the date of this Policy, you must not enter into margin lending arrangements using Origin Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security as a collateral against repayment of a loan, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.

detail: Granting security over Origin Securities to support any financing is prohibited as a 'secured financing arrangement'. A charge or lien unconnected to a financing is not named and is not a Dealing under the definition.
evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.

detail: Blanket ban on any secured financing in respect of Origin Securities, not limited to margin loans; no tier, security-state or approval carve-out and no exemption authority.
evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.

detail: Intention test: no acquisition with intent to dispose within three months, and no arrangements that result in short-term Dealing (margin loans given as an example). Carve-out for securities acquired on exercise of plan options/rights and shares acquired under employee equity incentive schemes.
evidence: You must not acquire Origin’s Securities with the intention of disposing or selling them within three months of acquisition, or enter into arrangements which result in short-term Dealing (such as margin loans) to minimise the perception of speculative trading.
